findings.title: Analytic-only sphere lights lack the BSDF-hit complement assumed by finite-light MIS
findings.details: The manifest loader creates LightComponent-only sphere entities. Sphere NEE uses non-delta area-to-solid-angle PDF and, except at the terminal path vertex, a power-heuristic MIS weight against the scattering PDF. Mesh miss evaluates only the environment; emitted radiance is read only at actual emissive mesh hits. The current sphere entities therefore have no corresponding BSDF-hit emitter contribution or TLAS occlusion. Guo spheres are geometric area emitters. Missing complement is established by source; image error magnitude and its share of any baseline residual are not established by this audit.
findings.limits: N3 is environment-only and is outside this finite-light finding. The earlier many-lights matched depth-1 control disables continuation MIS and does not test this issue. Smooth-conductor NEE is skipped, so reflected finite light also requires an actual emitter hit.

findings.title: Authored non-unit vertex normals interpolate differently
findings.details: The identity Assimp path retains supplied normal magnitudes; the engine interpolates them and then normalizes. Guo normalizes each vertex normal during PLY load, then interpolates. The original magnitudes vary strongly, so these operations produce different directions.
findings.limits: Predicted from source plus actual PLY data; the final imported GPU vertex buffer has not been captured. Audit does not attribute all rendered error to this difference.

findings.title: Guo and engine resolve geometric/shading hemisphere disagreement in opposite directions
findings.details: With provided vertex normals, Guo flipNormals negates vertex normals without reversing indices. At the actual triangle hit, Guo then flips the geometric normal toward the shading normal. The engine preserves the geometric cross and flips the interpolated shading normal toward it. Unitization plus a global flip alone cannot resolve the 16 triangles with mixed corner hemispheres.
findings.limits: Do not describe flipNormals as changing only the final shading frame: Guo hit-time alignment may also change the final geometric frame.

findings.title: Authored layer optical depth and generic microfacet alpha values are consistent
findings.details: Generic engine alpha is the authored roughness value, not its square. N3 has three surfaces with interface alphas 0.09 and 0.28 and absorption optical depths (0.0176,0.121,0.297) and (0.028,0.0032,0.0144). N4 has four surfaces, interface alphas 0.01,0.1,0.1, IOR sequence 1->1.5->1.1->1.5, absorption optical depths 0.25,0.15,0.1, and matching red/green diffuse terminals. The alpha01 name does not authorize changing the actual top alpha 0.01.
findings.limits: Layer count/optical depth alignment is not proof of identical stochastic BSDF PDF estimator, walk truncation, RR, global path-depth convention, or numerical acceptance. Prepared-run depth/camera/film contracts must be checked separately.

evaluated_alternatives.name: Shared smooth-normal control
evaluated_alternatives.assessment: A valid separate geometry-input control, not an unchanged authored baseline.
requirements: Keep all triangle positions and physical surfaces unchanged. Preserve original files.
Unitize authored normal directions and orient every per-triangle corner normal to the existing geometric face hemisphere; duplicate only corner records as necessary rather than enabling faceNormals.
Use exactly the same corrected PLY in both engines and Guo flipNormals=false. Verify all corner dot products are nonnegative, interpolation never vanishes, and the actual imported hit frames agree.
The correction changes the shading-normal field and may introduce local seams at malformed corners; disclose and measure it.

evaluated_alternatives.name: Paired emissive sphere mesh under existing finite-light convention
evaluated_alternatives.assessment: Approximation control only; not an exact scene-contract repair.
requirements: Existing Cornell area light pairs an emissive PLY with a LightComponent. A sphere analogue can supply emission hits and opaque visibility, but analytic NEE remains on a different surface.
All mesh facets must lie within the AreaLightPDFAtHit radial tolerance 1e-3; this only enables PDF recognition and does not make the analytic PDF/Jacobian exact for facets.

Prefer an audited convex inscribed hull; a visible analytic target segment lies outside that hull before origin offset. Test the actual PT_RAY_EPS=1e-4 offset and shortened segment at grazing angles; do not assume absence of self-shadow.
Quantify silhouette, area and radiance changes with at least two subdivision levels. Matching the Guo emitter to the same PLY still leaves engine analytic NEE versus mesh-surface sampling.

evaluated_alternatives.name: Exact analytic sphere emission-hit and shadow integration
evaluated_alternatives.assessment: Would address the missing renderer capability, but is a separate transport change requiring explicit scope approval.
requirements: Resolve nearest analytic sphere versus TLAS surface, evaluate emission with the same analytic PDF and light-selection PMF, and integrate sphere shadow blocking.
Preserve medium segment endpoints, primary versus continuation handling, and existing paired emissive mesh behavior without duplicate contribution.

Use focused actual-GPU negative and positive controls: black environment; diffuse and near-mirror receiver; depth1/2/16; emitter visibility; occlusion; matched Guo; independent seeds and noise/convergence.

post_render_independent_review: Accept only normal-exit completed batches with frozen source/input and output hash validation; preserve failed or incomplete attempts.
Verify scene-specific dimensions, SPP, seeds, path-depth mapping, camera/film and reference contract; do not inherit N2 settings silently.
Compute float64 spatial summaries per independent render first; run-level uncertainty uses independent seeds, not pixels as independent replicates.
Equal integer seed labels in different renderers do not establish paired random draws; engine/reference CI must use the independent-renderer method.
Use each scene-specific roi_precommit.json and validate bounds. Reject N2 sphere/central ROI hardcoded coordinates or masks inherited into shaderball/killeroo.
Separate coherent mean residual, raw SSIM, noise/variance and convergence; report actual gates and inconclusive outcomes. Noise compatibility does not prove zero bias.

A passing image metric cannot override known N4 source-contract failures. Keep radiance OPEN and stage_pass=false until explicitly resolved/accepted; no blanket stage PASS or fabricated visual approval.
